dimensions.assessment: Affects state and local governments, Indian Tribes, public-private partnerships, and communities receiving recycling infrastructure grants.
dimensions.evidence: States, local governments, Indian tribes, and public-private partnerships may apply for those grants.

dimensions.assessment: Provides funding opportunities up to $15 million per grant for eligible entities to improve local recycling accessibility, alongside new reporting obligations.
dimensions.evidence: A grant awarded to an eligible entity under the pilot grant program shall be in an amount--not less than $500,000; and not more than $15,000,000.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of $30 million annually for the grant program and $4 million annually for data collection across fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Administrator to carry out the pilot grant program $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029

dimensions.assessment: Directs the EPA to create a new pilot grant program, collect nationwide composting and recycling data, prepare periodic inventories, and develop new metrics.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator shall establish a pilot grant program, to be known as the 'Recycling Infrastructure and Accessibility Program'

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes five-year funding and establishes permanent statutory reporting and inventory requirements for the EPA and GAO.
dimensions.evidence: $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029

importance_detail.rationale: This bill establishes an EPA pilot grant program of $30 million annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2029, a $4 million annual data collection fund, inventory requirements, and reporting mandates involving state, local, and tribal governments.

card.summary: The Recycling Infrastructure and Accessibility Act of 2025 directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish a competitive pilot grant program to improve recycling accessibility in underserved communities using a hub-and-spoke model.
